This happened on Bajram day when the mosque was normally full of Albanians. At about 6.00 p.m. that evening, a local Serb neighbour," and so on and so forth and then you continue with that story. I'll avoid repeating that just to speed things up a little. And he said that you should leave and Mr. Ackerman asked you about that. Is that true, sir, what you said?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, it was 1155 hours on that day, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Excellent. At the Milosevic trial you also said in relation to this same event - and I'm curtailing this, I'll avoid reading the beginning. "On the 28th of March, at about 1155 hours he heard an explosion -- you heard an explosion. In the meantime, about five or six minutes later, along the road leading to Pristina, we saw a camouflage vehicle heading for Birac at a distance of 3 kilometres from Suva Reka where the military forces were stationed." Today you tell us that you saw a red military vehicle?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: No, I said camouflage. I didn't say red. It was patterned, I mean camouflaged, a Gazik. I did not say red.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if we look at today's transcript, page 47, lines 6 through 8, it reads: "A red vehicle, and the only vehicle moving at the time. It was coming from the direction of Birac and it was a military vehicle."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now, tell us, sir, which is true? The first time you gave evidence back in 2001 you made no reference whatsoever to seeing that vehicle at all. You only said you had heard from a neighbour that the Serbs had blown up the minaret. At the Milosevic trial you said that you had seen a camouflage vehicle. And today you say it was red. So which of the three different accounts is true?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: Today -- I don't know about the interpreting, but I did not mention the red. I said camouflage colour. I don't know that I mentioned red today. I don't know about the interpretation. I said Gazik formerly and I said today Gazik. So I'm repeating, a camouflage-colour vehicle, Gazik, in the direction of Birac. Maybe it was the interpretation. I never mentioned red -- the red colour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's enough to say it once. Mr. Bakrac, we'll have the interpretation checked, and you'll be told on -- once it's double-checked what the situation is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that was the interpretation I received. I see the same thing in the transcript; therefore, I have no reason to doubt the accuracy of this particular piece of interpretation. But we can have it checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, when you say "Gazik," what sort of a vehicle is that? Can you describe that vehicle for us, please.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: It's a Russian car. It's a Russian make car, but I never mentioned the red colour that you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is that a combat vehicle?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... with patterns.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did it have a cannon or something?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: No, camouflaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say "camouflaged," did it have a camouflage or was it just the camouflage colour?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: I meant camouflage colours, camouflage colours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, never until this day, not in your first statement which I've read out to you, not at the Milosevic trial, did you ever think to mention about your neighbour telling you or you having seen who was actually in that vehicle, yet today you tell us you saw the police and the army. Is this something you've just remembered today, sir?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: No. When I -- I rang them. My cousin is married to the Elshani family and to the Elshani family, and they had seen people in military uniform. I couldn't see the car, the vehicle, because they were inside a building and I couldn't see them from my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Excellent. You didn't see the vehicle. They told you what they saw inside the vehicle. When did they tell you that?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: I saw the car, but not the people inside the car. I saw the car on the 28th of March, 1999. It was two or three minutes after 1200 hours when it passed that way. At 1155 I heard the detonation, the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I am trying to wrap this up by 7.00. Please, give specific answers. I didn't ask you about the time you heard the explosion or anything like that. Please, try to focus on my questions. I asked you when you were told by your neighbours that they had noticed persons in military and police uniforms. When exactly were you told this by your neighbours, sir? Did they just tell you before you arrived in The Hague or what?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: That day, that same day on the 28th of March, 1999, it was about 12.00, a couple of minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... excellent. Now tell me why you never thought to mention this and yet you had at least three opportunities. Twice your statement was taken by OTP investigators. You told them about this specific event, about this specific vehicle, yet you never mentioned this, not at the Milosevic trial, either. If you had been told on the same day, why didn't you ever think to mention this to anyone until this very day?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: I said that I heard the explosion and I saw the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... what you heard. I'm asking you very specifically why today, for the very first time, after seven years you are telling us about a fact which you were specifically asked about. You had at least three opportunities to speak up.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: Well, there is the difference in time, of course, from 1999 till today, and maybe I've -- have forgotten something, minor details. Maybe then I did forget something and maybe today also.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Okay. So you've just remembered, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Berisha. What about those relatives of yours -- or you, because you're also on the record as saying that you actually saw the vehicle yourself. So did anyone actually see the vehicle stop and people being disgorged out of that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: I saw the car moving. Now, they went in the direction of Birac. It did not stop. When I saw the car, it was moving. Because it's only 300 metres from the mosque to my house, and the road leads to Birac. The car did not stop; it just went in the direction of Pristina and Birac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you actually see where it had started out from?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: The direction I saw, which was in the direction of Pristina. The direction -- they were heading towards Birac, from Pristina to Birac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, what I'm asking you is: Did you actually see this vehicle leave and where did it leave from?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: I couldn't see that -- I mean where it set off from. But I could see the car because it's an open area that you can see the car. I could see the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do understand that, Mr. Berisha, but there's something else I want to know, briefly, at least. I'm doing my best because we've only five minutes left. I'm trying to conclude my cross-examination, you see. Did your relatives see where the vehicle had come from or where it had started out from?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, their house is right there, close to the mosque, very close to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the location of their house; I am asking if they told you at the time where the vehicle had set out from.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. They started out from -- the vehicle started out from the mosque, from the vicinity of the mosque, in the direction of Birac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you've just remembered today of all days and you're telling us now for the very first time - right? - about them telling you that it had started out from outside the mosque?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: No, I said it even then that it started out from there. It started out from there, and it was -- the vehicle was seen because the mosque was very close, the car was parked near the mosque when the explosion happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When did you say that?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA
utterances.text: I said it then and I'm saying it today as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Would you like me to read the relevant portions on this event to you again? "In the meantime," and this is from the Milosevic transcript, "In the meantime, five or six minutes later, after you'd heard the explosion that is, along the road to Pristina we saw a camouflaged vehicle moving towards Birac, which is 3 kilometres from Suva Reka where the military forces were stationed. We saw that the mosque minaret in Suva Reka had been blown up. This was Bajram day, which was a Muslim holiday." This is the very transcript. You make no reference whatsoever there. You say five or six minutes after the explosion you saw this vehicle moving along, whereas in your statement dated the 17th of August, 2001, you say: "On the 28th of March, at about 1155 hours I heard an explosion and saw that the minaret had been blown up. I called a relative on the phone who lived near the mosque and he told me that the Serbs had blown up the minaret. This happened on Bajram day," and so on and so forth. Never so far have you mentioned the fact that your relatives told you about the vehicle setting out from outside the mosque, have you? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Maybe I could ask for a reference -- it was my understanding from the Milosevic transcript that -- that the relatives did see the vehicle outside the mosque, but maybe I'm missing what the point is, but that was my understanding. The second thing I'd like to -- we have requested to make --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just -- I understand -- I know what you want to do. Just sit down and I'll deal with procedural things as and when it's convenient. All right. That would not have been a good reason for interrupting anyone's cross-examination. Now, Mr. Bakrac, this is too complicated a question for tonight. It's really not a helpful way to try and get to the basis -- for example, I don't at the moment know whether the part you've quoted from the Milosevic trial was cross-examination, nor have you -- is it clear to me whether the question was ever asked. So it's -- it's not really terribly helpful, but you can reflect overnight on whether there might be a better way of asking the question to try and assist your own case, bearing in mind what answers you've been securing so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you just allow me a second, Your Honour. He was a 92 bis witness, he was heard as a 92 bis witness -- or rather, his statement was read out, the statement that I'm quoting. Everything apart from that was in cross-examination at the Milosevic trial. What this means is his statement was read out by the OTP. No additional questions, and they started the cross-examination right away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So whenever you refer to his answers they're in cross-examination, which puts an entirely different impression on -- on them. It depends what the question was and what the questioner was trying to achieve. However, you can address the matter again tomorrow. Now, Ms. Carter, I understand you have an application to make.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution is seeking to amend the 65 ter summary of the following witness, Ali Gjogaj. Apparently the materials were disclosed to the Defence with regards to this 92 bis package first in case number 9937 to the original MOS defendants on the 30th of January, 2003. The materials were then disclosed to the final defendants on June 30th, 2005, under thousand number 0370. They were also a part of the 92 bis package that was filed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let me know, first of all, what it is you want to do. I mean, there's no point in giving me all this information until I know what the application is. I know it's to vary the 65 ter summary, but I need to know in what respect before anything else makes any sense to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. There needs to be an additional paragraph added to the 65 ter list. When the 65 ter was originally drafted it appears to only be referencing the first statement of the witness and is completely silent as to the second statement of the witness, which we do intend to lead evidence on. There also needs to be a correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So, how has that happened?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I cannot speak to who originally drafted the 65 ter list. Once this attorney became aware of the witness and became responsible for this witness, I began to go through the materials and make amendments as quickly as possible. This has only come to light to me very recently, and as soon as that did come to light, I began making procedures to put the Defence on notice. The Defence was given the last break a proposal for the 65 ter amendment in order to put them on notice about the arguments that are going to be made here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So what -- we've a whole statement of the witness that isn't heralded in your 65 ter summary? Is that -- that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And when did you become aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Frankly, Your Honour, the materials came to this attorney yesterday. And once I received the materials, I began making all possible checks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you see, you would really need to be able to explain to us why this situation had arisen in the first place, which at the moment you don't appear to be able to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've tried to do some investigation to figure out what exactly happened. This appears to be the first 65 ter summary that was also being used in Milosevic, which is actually surprising to this attorney because in the Milosevic case the entire 92 bis package was brought into Court, which did include the second statement. The witness was cross-examined on it. It appears at all times that the entire -- both statements had been at issue, but for whatever reason in the Milosevic trial and then beginning into this trial, the 65 ter summary was not complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, the statement is dated the 24th -- is it the 24th of June statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it was only a few short months after the original statement was taken, so it's unclear why it is not a part of the original 65 ter summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what is it that it deals with that is not in the existing summary?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: It most directly goes to paragraph 75(d) of the indictment, Your Honour, it's dealing with the removal of bodies from the artillery field that is in issue here in Suva Reka --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The first statement does that as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: No, actually, Your Honour, that deals with Pusto Selo which was several -- that removal was several weeks after the artillery range was addressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, do you have the proposed amendment to your 65 ter summary to give me?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have it in hard copy form. Ms. Grogan can tender it to the assistants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And this you've already given to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, they were given this in the last break. The portions that are at issue is the final paragraph which I've bolded to be able to draw it to the attention of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, Mr. Berisha, we have no more time this evening to hear any further evidence, so that means that you will have to come back tomorrow to continue your evidence. We will be resuming at 2.15 tomorrow, so you need to be back here able to begin giving evidence at 2.15. Between now and then, it's vital that you should not discuss your evidence with anyone, and that means the evidence you've already given and the evidence you may yet give in the case. You can talk about anything else to whoever you like, but don't talk about the evidence. Okay. So you can now leave the courtroom and we'll see you tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You should have an opportunity, Ms. Carter, to try and provide us with more information to explain why this has happened, and I'll hear you again before we commence further with this witness tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 21st day of September, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.
